samples.summary: Soft-wait rationale (in both code comment and the design doc) rests on a mechanism the harness does not exercise. The comment says `FONT_CATALOG`'s eager set is "registered on slides/docs mounts" and that the quiet wait "is what actually catches a late-injected per-family link (ThemedFontPicker)", but `ensureGoogleFontsLink`/`useGoogleFontsLink` are only called from `SlidesView` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:230) and `DocsView`, and `ThemedFontPicker` explicitly states "nothing to do here" (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/themed-font-picker.tsx:39-40). The visual harness renders the pickers standalone and never calls either, and `grep` over `src/app/harness` finds no `ensureFontLink`/`useGoogleFontsLink`/`FONT_CATALOG` use. The added `FONT_QUIET_TIMEOUT_MS` machinery and the matching paragraph in docs/design/harness-engineering.md therefore document a load path that does not occur in this lane.

`REQUIRED_WEB_FONTS` hand-duplicates the css2 query in packages/frontend/index.html:12 (and the identical query in packages/documentation/.vitepress/config.ts:24), kept in sync only by a comment. The task doc's own "Follow-up" section names hand-kept family lists as a prior failure mode; deriving the floor from the `<link href>` (or asserting equality in a unit test) would remove the drift the comment asks a human to police. Nothing in the repo checks the two agree.

The gate floor covers only index.html's three families, so any web family a baseline actually paints but index.html does not request is now downgraded to a 3s warn-only wait. `slides-pickers` — one of the two targets in the originating issue — renders every entry of SYSTEM_FONTS (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/themed-font-picker-helpers.ts:12, incl. "Roboto" and "Lora", both Google families) with `style={{ fontFamily: family }}`, and slide/theme scenarios render theme heading/body families. If any of those resolve to a web face in some run and a fallback in another, the exact drift class the issue was filed for can recur while the lane only warns. Worth confirming that no non-floor family in a captured target ever resolves to a webfont.

Sibling capture script still uses a bare `document.fonts.ready`, i.e. the exact weakness this change removes from the visual lane. The task doc lists it as a known limitation, so this is only a reuse/consistency note: the settle logic is now non-trivial and lives inline in verify-visual-browser.mjs rather than in a shared helper both scripts could call.

verdict.reason:
The finding's premise — that a captured target paints a *web* face for a family outside the `REQUIRED_WEB_FONTS` floor (it names Roboto and Lora in `slides-pickers`, and theme heading/body families) — does not hold in this repository.

1. The only Google Fonts stylesheet ever present on the visual-harness page is `index.html`'s, which requests exactly Fraunces / Inter / JetBrains Mono (packages/frontend/index.html:12) — i.e. exactly the floor in verify-visual-browser.mjs:374-378.
2. The eager catalog bundle (which is where Roboto lives — font-catalog.data.ts:49 `eager: true`) is injected only by `ensureGoogleFontsLink()`, and that function's sole callers are `useGoogleFontsLink()` (font-catalog.ts:195-199), used only in `DocsView` (docs-view.tsx:210) and `SlidesView` (slides-view.tsx:230). Neither view is mounted by the harness: `harness/visual/page.tsx:1-27` imports only the five scenario modules, and grepping `SlidesView|DocsView|useGoogleFontsLink|ensureGoogleFontsLink|ensureFontLink` across `src/app/harness/**` returns no matches. So Roboto has no `@font-face` registered during capture.
3. Lora is a *non-eager* catalog entry (font-catalog.data.ts:52), fetched only via `ensureFontLink`, whose call sites are all user-driven: `FontFamilyPicker` `onPointerEnter` prefetch (font-family-picker.tsx:177,205), `applySlideFontFamily` (apply-font-family.ts:28), theme-builder `setFont` (theme-builder-panel.tsx:99-101), docs apply handler, and the "More fonts…" in-view prefetch. `capturePass` (verify-visual-browser.mjs:571-609) performs no pointer/click interaction, and `ThemeBuilderPanel`/`MoreFontsDialog` are not in any scenario.
4. `ThemedFontPicker` itself injects nothing — themed-font-picker.tsx:39-40 explicitly states it relies on the link that `SlidesView` would inject. The `slides-pickers` scenario renders the picker standalone with `PICKER_THEME = defaultLight` (slides-scenarios.tsx:907, 1813-1828).

So the Roboto/Lora/system rows resolve to locally-installed or fallback faces deterministically (no network), and cannot flip between a webfont and a fallback across runs — the drift class the issue was filed for cannot recur through them. Separately, the originating task doc itself specifies this exact design: "Demote everything else to a non-gating, shorter (3s) wait for quiet ... that warns instead of failing" (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:112-114), so the diff conforms to its acceptance criteria rather than violating one. The residual note about a hypothetical future non-floor webfont is a `minor` maintenance caveat, not a blocking design-fit defect.

finding.summary: Deriving the wait set from `document.fonts` turns every registered family into a hard gate, widening the lane's dependency on fonts.googleapis.com far beyond the families a capture actually paints. The bootstrap link (`buildGoogleFontsHref`, font-catalog.data.ts) registers ~8 eager families (Noto Sans/Serif KR, Nanum Gothic, Nanum Myeongjo, Gothic A1, Gowun Dodum/Batang, Roboto) plus index.html's Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, on every page load of every slides/docs section. The new `load()` forces a woff2 fetch for each of them and `pending()` then requires each to reach `loaded`, so a transient CDN failure on a Korean family that appears in no screenshot now fails the whole visual run (exit 1 at the end) even when all 220 targets match pixel-for-pixel. The originating issue's outcome was to stop a font race from producing wrong screenshots; this approach adds a new, broader flake/failure surface and sits against the doc's Goal 'Keep verification deterministic and reproducible between local and CI' (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:121). Scoping the gate to the families the captured targets actually render (or the vendoring the task doc lists as out of scope) would fit the issue better.
finding.evidence: pending(): `if (!statuses.includes("loaded")) missing.push(...)` applied to every family in `registry()`, which is built from all of `document.fonts`.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism is not in the code. It claims the wait set is derived from document.fonts via registry()/pending(), making every registered family (the ~8 eager Korean/Roboto catalog families from buildGoogleFontsHref, plus KaTeX faces) a hard gate. No registry() or pending() function exists in the script (repo-wide grep for "registry()" hits only vendored zod under .trusted/). The actual gate is missingRequired() at verify-visual-browser.mjs:437-462, which iterates `for (const { family, weights } of required)` where `required` is the hard-coded 3-entry constant REQUIRED_WEB_FONTS (:374-378) = Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono — exactly the css2 query at packages/frontend/index.html:12, i.e. the families the baselines were recorded with and which index.html already requests on every page load. The quoted evidence line `if (!statuses.includes("loaded"))` is real (:450) but sits inside that three-family loop, not over the registry; facesFor() (:414-415) only reads document.fonts to filter for those three families. loadRequired() (:422-435) likewise force-loads only the floor, with an explicit comment (:417-421) stating that forcing every registered family would wrongly pull in KaTeX's italic-only faces and the eager catalog families. The one registry-wide read, stillLoading() (:466-472), is non-gating by construction: when missing is empty, a non-empty loading produces only a console.warn "capturing anyway" (:534-541) and never pushes to webFontFailures; only floor misses reach webFontFailures (:546, :556), which is what drives the exit 1 at :821-823. So the described scenario — a transient CDN failure on a Korean family that appears in no screenshot failing the whole run — cannot occur: those families are never force-loaded and never checked for "loaded". The design-fit argument (over-broad fonts.googleapis.com dependency, tension with the determinism Goal) rests entirely on the widened wait set, which does not exist.
